stories.headline: Israel votes Tuesday, and nobody is winning yet
body: Israel holds a national election on Tuesday, 27 October, and the final polls show no clear winner.
TV polls give Prime Minister Netanyahu's camp about 50 seats and the opposition about 52, both short of the 61 needed to govern.
Gadi Eisenkot's new Yashar party leads most polls, with Netanyahu's Likud close behind.
stories.joke: Final polls: 50 vs 52 out of 120. Coalition talks may outlast the campaign.
stories.vc: A long coalition fight can keep Israel's markets and its huge tech sector cautious. Watch the shekel and Israeli startup funding after the vote.

stories.statLabel: pulled out of Indian shares in October
stories.headline: Foreign investors keep pulling money out of India
body: Foreign investors pulled ₹48,056 crore out of Indian shares in October so far.
That takes 2026's total to about ₹3.08 lakh crore, already far more than all of 2025.
Costly oil, war worries and weaker company earnings are the main reasons, though selling eased late in the week.
stories.joke: 2026 is the year foreign funds told India: it's not you, it's oil.
stories.vc: When foreign money leaves, valuations cool and good companies get cheaper. Patient local investors and family offices can buy quality at better prices.

stories.headline: Year-old AI lab with no product raises $1 billion
body: Flapping Airplanes, an AI research lab founded in late 2025, raised $1 billion at a $6 billion valuation.
Index Ventures and Lux Capital led the round, with Sequoia, GV, Kleiner Perkins and Nvidia also joining.
Its team of a couple dozen people works on training AI with less data and computing power, and has no product or revenue yet.
stories.joke: No product, no revenue, $6 billion. Somewhere a profitable kirana store is rethinking its life choices.
stories.vc: Top funds are paying frontier prices for AI 'neolabs' on team and idea alone. That raises the bar for what strong early AI founders can ask for.

stories.headline: Strong 7.0 quake shakes Japan's Ogasawara Islands
body: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck near Japan's Ogasawara Islands on Sunday morning, Japan's weather agency said.
It hit very deep, about 470 km below the surface, and no tsunami warning was issued.
It was felt across eastern Japan, and early reports showed no injuries or damage.
stories.vc: Japan is a key supplier of chips, machines and parts. Even quakes without damage are a reminder to keep backup suppliers in your supply chain.

stories.headline: Infosys profit rises 6%, but it trims its growth forecast
body: Infosys made a profit of ₹7,823 crore in July to September, up about 6% from a year ago.
Revenue grew about 11% to ₹49,244 crore, and the board declared a dividend of ₹26 per share.
But it now expects revenue to grow only 1% to 2% this year, a sign that clients are still careful with tech spending.
stories.joke: Dividend up, forecast down: the IT sector's favourite way of saying 'it's complicated.'
stories.vc: Slow growth at India's IT giants means services alone won't drive the next decade. The opportunity shifts to AI products and tools that make these firms more efficient.

stories.headline: Jim Keller's chip startup Tenstorrent raises $1.5 billion
body: AI chip startup Tenstorrent raised $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion valuation, more than double its value in 2024.
Trace Capital and Innovation X led the round, with ARK Invest, Fidelity and T. Rowe Price joining.
It had explored a sale to Intel and Qualcomm this year, but chose to stay independent and build more of its Galaxy servers.
stories.joke: Said no to Intel and Qualcomm, then raised $1.5 billion. Peak 'I'm not leaving, I'm upgrading' energy.
stories.vc: Investors are funding Nvidia challengers at scale. Cheaper, more open AI hardware could cut costs for every startup that rents computing power.

stories.headline: British Columbia's snap election hands Conservatives a majority
body: Canada's British Columbia province voted on Saturday, and the B.C. Conservatives won a majority government.
With most ballots counted, they led in 62 of 93 seats, against 29 for Premier David Eby's NDP.
Eby had called the early election himself, and he said he will step down as NDP leader.
stories.joke: Calling a snap election to win bigger is bold. So is calling one and losing the job.
stories.vc: B.C. is home to Canada's big Pacific ports, mines and forests. A new government could speed up resource and energy projects, worth watching for supply chains.

stories.headline: Smallcaps suffer their worst week in 20 months
body: Indian smallcap shares fell about 7% in the week to 23 October, their worst week since February 2025.
The Nifty Smallcap 100 dropped 7.3% and the Midcap 100 lost 5.6%.
Costly oil, war worries, fears of interest rate rises and high prices for small stocks all pushed investors to sell.
stories.joke: Smallcap investors learned the difference between 'long term' and 'long week.'
stories.vc: Sharp falls flush out speculative money. That is often when patient investors find good small companies at fair prices.

stories.headline: Xona raises $250 million to build a rival to GPS
body: Xona Space Systems raised $250 million at a $2.45 billion valuation to build a new satellite navigation network.
Its Pulsar satellites sit in low Earth orbit, and it pitches them as an answer to growing GPS jamming and spoofing.
Six satellites launched on 20 October, and it plans to start commercial service in 2027.
stories.joke: Finally, a GPS alternative. Now if only it could find parking in Bengaluru.
stories.vc: Navigation is critical infrastructure for defence, shipping and phones. Space startups selling to governments and big industry are drawing late-stage money.

stories.headline: Iran's president heads to Moscow to meet Putin
body: Iran's foreign minister said President Masoud Pezeshkian will travel to Moscow next week to meet Vladimir Putin.
Iran's ambassador said the visit is tied to a summit of gas-exporting countries on Tuesday, 27 October.
It would be his first trip to Russia to meet Putin since the conflict involving Iran began.
stories.joke: Two heavily sanctioned gas giants, meeting at a gas summit. The small talk writes itself.
stories.vc: Closer Iran-Russia ties can keep oil and gas prices jumpy. For an Indian manufacturer, energy and freight costs are the lines to watch.

stories.statLabel: govt stake in Punjab & Sind Bank
stories.headline: Government plans to sell part of its stake in four state banks
body: The government is considering selling shares in four state-run banks to cut its stake to 75%, reports say.
The banks are Central Bank of India, UCO Bank, Punjab & Sind Bank and Indian Overseas Bank, where it owns 81% to 94% today.
The sales would likely happen on the stock market within about a year, to meet the rule that at least 25% of shares be public.
stories.joke: Owning 94% of a listed bank is the government's 'it's complicated' relationship status.
stories.vc: Stake sales add share supply but can bring more market discipline to state banks. Watch the pricing; discounts often reward early buyers.

stories.headline: Ex-OpenAI science chief raises $215M for robot drug labs
body: Kevin Weil, who led science work at OpenAI, launched Warp Sciences with a $215 million first funding round led by Lightspeed.
It will make and test new molecules for drug companies in US labs, using chemists, AI and robots.
The aim is to bring back lab work that drugmakers have long sent to contractors in China.
stories.joke: AI designs it, robots mix it, chemists check it. The lab coat is now a dashboard.
stories.vc: This is 'picks and shovels' for biotech plus a supply-chain shift away from China. India's chemistry research firms should watch closely.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drones hit a chemical plant deep in Siberia
body: Drones struck the Omsky Kauchuk chemical plant and an Ozon warehouse in Omsk, Siberia, more than 2,400 km from Ukraine, on 24 October.
The plant makes synthetic rubber and a petrol additive, and reports said it caught fire.
Ukraine's military also said it hit a big rubber plant in Tolyatti, in central Russia, the same day.
stories.vc: Strikes on Russian refineries and chemical plants keep global fuel and rubber supply tight. Tyre, auto and plastics makers feel it in their input costs.

stories.headline: Adani Power's profit jumps 142%, helped by a one-time boost
body: Adani Power's profit rose 142% to ₹7,019 crore in July to September, from ₹2,906 crore a year earlier.
About ₹2,422 crore came from a one-time revision of old power charges, while higher demand and tariffs also helped.
Revenue grew about 30% to ₹17,014 crore, and its debt stood at ₹61,860 crore.
stories.joke: 142% growth, one-time edition. Next quarter's sequel may need a better script.
stories.vc: Look past headline profit to repeatable earnings. India's power demand story is real, but one-time gains can flatter the numbers.

stories.headline: Fusion startup Helion lines up $225 million for power chips
body: Fusion energy startup Helion signed a letter of intent for up to $175 million from the US government's CHIPS programme.
It also raised $50 million from a private investor, and the government would get a small non-voting stake.
The money will fund new power chips that Helion says could double the output of its fusion machines.
stories.joke: The plan: build a small sun. The bottleneck: chips. Some things never change.
stories.vc: Deep-tech bets now mix venture money with government cheques. Founders in energy and chips should learn to raise from both.

stories.headline: South Africa's trade with China jumps after tariffs are dropped
body: Trade between South Africa and China reached nearly $15 billion from May to August, up about 24% from a year ago.
China removed import taxes on goods from 53 African countries in May, and South Africa's exports to China rose about 25%.
Farm exports jumped more than 35%, but South Africa still buys far more from China than it sells.
stories.joke: Zero tariffs: the only zero everyone in trade is happy to see.
stories.vc: Tariff-free access to China changes the maths for African farm and mining exporters. Trade-linked businesses across Africa get a new growth lane.

stories.statLabel: Series B led by Khosla Ventures
stories.headline: Bengaluru's Even Healthcare raises $50M to build hospitals
body: Bengaluru-based Even Healthcare raised $50 million in a round led by its existing investor, Khosla Ventures.
It will use the money to open five new hospitals in Bengaluru over the next six months.
Its doctors earn fixed salaries, with bonuses tied to patient results rather than the number of procedures.
stories.joke: A hospital that earns more when you need it less. Your gym has used this model for years.
stories.vc: Even bets on fixing incentives in Indian healthcare, a huge and broken market. Watch whether its membership model scales beyond Bengaluru.

stories.statLabel: km of metro, at launch vs now
stories.headline: Namma Metro turns 15 and aims beyond 100 km
body: Bengaluru's Namma Metro has completed 15 years of passenger service.
It has grown from a 6.7 km line to about 96 km, and plans to cross 100 km.
Its 57 original trains are getting their first major overhaul, but the city's traffic jams have not gone away.
stories.joke: 15 years of metro, and Bengaluru traffic is still undefeated.
stories.vc: Metro lines reshape where people live and work. Real estate, retail and logistics near new stations tend to gain first.

stories.headline: Rural health startup CureBay raises ₹100 crore
body: Bhubaneswar-based CureBay raised about ₹100 crore in a round led by IvyCap Ventures.
That is ₹69 crore in equity and over ₹30 crore in debt, and part of it will fund a move into Andhra Pradesh.
CureBay runs more than 250 clinics in seven states, helped by over 1,800 local health workers.
stories.joke: Healthcare that comes to the village, instead of the village taking a bus to the city.
stories.vc: Rural health is big and underserved. Mixing equity with venture debt lets founders grow without giving away too much of the company.

stories.headline: Mexico's economy grows faster than expected
body: Mexico's economic output grew 3.3% in the year to August, above the 3.1% that forecasters expected.
Mexican shares were steady and the peso firmed at the end of the week.
Diesel buyers got no tax relief for a sixth week in a row.
stories.joke: Mexico beat forecasts. Economists are now forecasting by how much it will beat forecasts.
stories.vc: Mexico gains as companies move factories closer to the US. For Indian manufacturers it is both a rival and a partner market.
